headline: Meta to issue new shares to fund AI push, acquisitions
summary: The company plans to issue non-voting stock starting in 2027, expanding its funding tools for AI investments and strategic initiatives.
details: Meta announced plans to create a new class of non-voting shares, primarily to fund its aggressive artificial intelligence initiatives. These shares are slated to begin trading in 2027.

The company stated that the new share class will also be used for potential acquisitions and to compensate employees. This move aims to provide Meta with greater financial flexibility to invest in AI, which is transforming the industry.

Meta's Chief Financial Officer, Susan Li, highlighted that the new shares will "expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI."

This financial strategy comes as Meta pours billions into its AI race, including building data centers, hiring top talent, and developing advanced AI models. The company anticipates capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year.
The announcement follows a busy period for Meta, which recently launched its AI agent, Muse, in September. Muse has achieved over 10 million downloads in the US and hit the top of app stores.

However, Muse has faced some challenges, including privacy concerns after a user reported the agent revealed his address. Meta also paused a feature that made user chats publicly available on the web.
